answer: Suya is a Nigerian grilled-meat dish associated especially with Hausa food traditions in northern Nigeria. Thin pieces of meat are coated with yaji, a spicy dry seasoning often made with groundnut cake, chilli and other aromatics, then grilled over high heat. It is commonly served with onions, tomatoes and extra seasoning.

facts.fact: A 2023 peer-reviewed review identifies suya or tsire-suya as originating in northern Nigeria and now found across the country.
The 2023 review describes yaji-kuli-kuli and charcoal grilling as characteristic parts of suya.
The Washington Post's 30 September 2021 article describes groundnut-based yaji on thin meat skewers.
The Guardian published a UK-focused suya cultural feature on 13 November 2022.
Immaculate Bites published a 2022 oven/grill adaptation of suya.
Serious Eats has a Nigerian beef suya recipe describing a seasoned grilled-skewer preparation.
